source: World Health Organization - Essential Medicines and Health Products
description: WHO treatment protocols for common conditions in resource-limited settings

protocols.confirmation: Test before treat when possible (RDT or microscopy)

artemisinin_based_combination_therapy.adults: Artemether-lumefantrine (AL) or Artesunate-amodiaquine or Artesunate-mefloquine or Dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine
artemisinin_based_combination_therapy.children: Same as adults, dosed by weight
artemisinin_based_combination_therapy.pregnant_women: First trimester: Quinine + Clindamycin. Second/third trimester: ACT recommended

dosing.artemether_lumefantrine: Tablets: 20mg/120mg - 4 tablets at 0,8,24,36,48,60 hours (6 doses over 3 days)

severe_malaria.treatment: Parenteral artesunate preferred (IV/IM). Alternative: Artemether IM or Quinine IV
severe_malaria.quinine_dosing: 20mg/kg loading dose IV over 4 hours, then 10mg/kg every 8 hours
severe_malaria.when_to_switch: When patient can tolerate oral medication, complete with 3-day ACT course

prevention.itns: Insecticide-treated bed nets for all at-risk persons
prevention.irs: Indoor residual spraying in high-transmission areas
prevention.iptp: Intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy: Sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (SP) at each scheduled antenatal visit after quickening
prevention.smc: Seasonal malaria chemoprevention in Sahel sub-region: Sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine + Amodiaquine monthly during rainy season for children 3-59 months

protocols.treatment_initiation: All adults and adolescents living with HIV should start ART as soon as possible after diagnosis, regardless of CD4 count, clinical stage, or WHO clinical criteria

adults_adolescents.first_line: Tenofovir (TDF or TAF) + Lamivudine (3TC) or Emtricitabine (FTC) + Dolutegravir (DTG)

children.14-25kg: TDF + 3TC + DTG or ABC + 3TC + DTG or LPV/r

monitoring.baseline: CD4 count, HIV viral load (if available), Hemoglobin, ALT/AST, Cr, Hepatitis B/C serology, STI screening, Cervical cancer screening (women)
monitoring.follow_up: Clinical assessment every 3-6 months, Viral load at 6 months after starting ART then annually
monitoring.success_criteria: Viral suppression (<1000 copies/mL) by 6 months on ART

prevention.prep: Daily oral PrEP for people at substantial risk of HIV infection
prevention.pmtct: Option B+: All pregnant and breastfeeding women with HIV receive lifelong ART with Tenofovir + 3TC/FTC + DTG or EFV
prevention.pep: 28-day course of TDF + 3TC (or FTC) + DTG (or boosted PI) started as soon as possible after exposure, ideally within 72 hours

new_patients.intensive_phase: 2 months: Isoniazid (H) 5mg/kg (max 300mg) + Rifampicin (R) 10mg/kg (max 600mg) + Pyrazinamide (Z) 25mg/kg (max 2g) + Ethambutol (E) 15mg/kg daily under DOT
new_patients.continuation_phase: 4 months: INH + RIF daily or 3 times weekly under DOT

adjustments.extrapulmonary: Extend continuation phase to 7 months (9 months total)
adjustments.cavitary_pulmonary: Consider extending continuation phase to 7 months if sputum positive at 2 months

previously_treated.regimen: 8 months: 2SHRZE/1HRZE/5HRE or shorter regimens based on DST
previously_treated.note: Use rapid molecular DST to guide regimen selection

rif_resistant.duration: 6 months (extend to 9 months for extensive disease)

drug_resistant_tb.multidrug_resistant: Individualized regimens based on DST, include Group A (Levofloxacin/Moxifloxacin, Bedaquiline, Linezolid) plus Group B and C drugs

regimens: 6 or 9 months isoniazid (300mg daily or twice weekly)
3 months weekly isoniazid + rifapentine (3HP) - not in all countries

infection_control: Use of particulate respirators in high-risk settings

diseases.name: Soil-transmitted helminths
diseases.treatment: Albendazole 400mg single dose or Mebendazole 500mg single dose
diseases.preventive_chemotherapy: Annual or biannual mass drug administration in endemic areas

diseases.name: Lymphatic filariasis
diseases.treatment: Annual mass drug administration: Albendazole 400mg + Ivermectin 150-200mcg/kg or DEC 6mg/kg

diseases.name: Onchocerciasis
diseases.note: Contraindicated in children <5 years or <15kg, pregnant women, and severely ill patients

diseases.name: Trachoma
diseases.treatment: Annual mass drug administration: Azithromycin 20mg/kg (max 1g) single oral dose for 3 years

priority_diseases.schedule: First dose at 9 months, second dose at 15-18 months (or before school entry)

Birth (OPV0), 6 weeks (OPV1 + Pentavalent 1 + PCV 1 + IPV), 10 weeks (OPV2 + Pentavalent 2 + PCV 2 + RV 2), 14 weeks (OPV3 + Pentavalent 3 + PCV 3 + IPV + RV 3), 9 months (Measles R1 + Yellow fever), 18 months (Measles R2 + DPT booster)
Single dose at 9 months (endemic countries), provides lifelong immunity
Single dose 1-29 years in meningitis belt countries during campaigns

supplementation: Vitamin A every 4-6 months for children 6-59 months
Iron and folic acid supplementation for pregnant women and children as per national policy
